name: Neo-Legionarism
summary: Neo-Legionarism is the post-1989 Romanian movement that claims to continue the interwar Iron Guard of Corneliu Zelea Codreanu. It combines ethnic nationalism, intense Orthodox religiosity and mysticism, antisemitism, anti-communism and hostility to liberal democracy, the EU and NATO. It aims at a spiritual rebirth of the nation, a restored Greater Romania and rule by a morally formed elite around a leader cult.
scope: The post-communist neo-Legionary current (Noua Dreapta, Legionary-successor groups, Prison Saints devotion) as documented since the 1990s, anchored in Codreanu's For My Legionaries and early Guard of the National Conscience creed. It excludes the interwar Legion in power and electoral populists such as AUR who deny the label; economic answers are mostly inferred from the creed and third-position claims.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Codreanu's early creed promised homes for invalids and a risk fund for workers, so state care fits; healthcare itself is never discussed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 1920 creed wanted wages scaled to work and family size and reduced class differences; a wage floor is inferred from that.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Noua Dreapta rejects capitalism as well as Marxism and the creed subordinates enterprise to the nation, so free markets are not trusted to allocate.

public-ownership.rationale: The early creed called for nationalizing factories, but later Legionary and neo-Legionary writing is mostly silent on economics.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The creed endorsed a progressive income tax; modern groups add little on tax.

unions-good.rationale: Codreanu organised national unions of workers, but as nationalist bodies opposed to Marxist unions, so support is conditional.

property-fundamental.rationale: The creed backs private initiative only where it serves the nation, which makes property subordinate to national interest.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Neo-Legionaries attack international companies, and the creed has the state guarantee workers' shares and limit owners' returns.

cut-welfare.rationale: The creed's social provisions (risk fund, storehouses, homes for the old) point against cutting welfare, though it was written for citizens only.

worker-ownership.rationale: The creed proposes nationalized or state-backed firms with worker representation, not collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A movement that sees a hidden conspiracy against the nation would accept security measures; inferred, not documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Neo-Legionarism is documented as opposing drugs alongside homosexuality and abortion.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents have been prosecuted under laws on Legionary symbols and denial and see them as censorship, but they would curb what they call Judaic press power.

strong-leader.rationale: Codreanu says he never put propositions to a vote and chose his followers himself; the Captain principle is the movement's core.

state-harmful.rationale: The Legion wanted a stronger, purified Romanian state, not its abolition (the creed speaks of one undivided state).

limit-guns.rationale: The sources show no position; the Legion valued armed discipline but nothing addresses civilian gun law.

empower-police-military.rationale: The creed treats the army as a school of the nation, and order-minded nationalism favours more authority, though inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Orthodox moral campaign against homosexuality, drugs and what it calls immorality.

decide-locally.rationale: The creed demands one undivided Romanian state from the Dniester to the Tisa, so decisions stay national.

rehabilitation.rationale: No stated penal doctrine; the cult of prison martyrs treats prison as suffering that tests the pure, and a punitive line is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The creed names the state protector of the family and neo-Legionaries oppose homosexuality and abortion.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Both Wikipedia articles document opposition to homosexuality and anti-LGBT marches by Noua Dreapta.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposition to abortion is documented for neo-Legionary groups and on Noua Dreapta's own website.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement is built on Orthodox religion in politics; Codreanu's creed demands a Sacred Christian Church of the nation.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: An ethnic-nationalist movement opposes human-rights framing and treats minorities as threats.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Neo-Legionaries criticize gender and human-rights agendas and defend traditional roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving the national spirit and traditions of interwar Romania is the movement's stated purpose.

gradual-change.rationale: It seeks a spiritual revolution and a new man, not gradual change, though some figures favor legal routes.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Expelling immigrants is a documented neo-Legionary demand and Noua Dreapta rallied against refugees.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The UN, NATO and the EU are named among threats, and internationalism is condemned.

free-trade.rationale: Criticism of international companies and open borders suggests protectionism; trade is not discussed directly.

nation-first.rationale: Ethnic nationalism and hostility to internationalism put national interest first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Hostile to human-rights discourse and international bodies; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Neo-Legionary writing condemns internationalism as eroding national borders, and the movement wants immigrants expelled.

limit-growth.rationale: Not an environmental movement, but its anti-modern, spiritual outlook gives it little commitment to growth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Sovereigntist and hostile to international bodies that coordinate climate policy; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The movement frames politics as spiritual struggle, so technology as a cure is unlikely; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; a nationalism that prizes self-sufficiency would favour domestic energy, so this is inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Adherents speak of a spiritual revolution and the Legion used violence, though modern groups mostly shifted to civil-society and electoral forms.

experts-over-public.rationale: The creed would put the nation's moral soldiers in charge rather than technocrats or the public; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Third-position and corporatist economics rejects both capitalism and communism, so full planning is out.

socialized-markets.rationale: Noua Dreapta rejects Marxism, and public or worker ownership is not part of the program.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source addresses a land tax; the movement has no stated fiscal doctrine beyond the creed's progressive income tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No stated position; the creed's progressive income tax is the only hint.

basic-income.rationale: The creed ties pay to work performed, so an unconditional income is unlikely.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The creed has the state own factories and run a risk fund, implying direction of the economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The creed distributes land among ploughmen and Codreanu defends the peasant and middle class against Jewish commerce.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The creed itself pays wages and salaries, and the movement is anti-communist.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Hostile to finance and usury, but no source gives a monetary doctrine, so adherents are not clearly for abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The creed has national unions with representatives on the administrative boards of firms, a corporatist design.

one-party-rule.rationale: Codreanu rejected party politics but the Legion sought exclusive national leadership; inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Codreanu's early creed praised King Ferdinand yet the Legion later clashed with the crown; adherents are not united.

democracy-best.rationale: Codreanu: democracy was excluded and he lived anti-democracy from the start; the democratic setup is a curse on the people.

direct-votes.rationale: He never put propositions to a vote, and rejects voting as manipulated by Jewish money and press.

workers-councils.rationale: Anti-communist and committed to national unions under national leadership.

right-to-secede.rationale: The creed demands one undivided state and the movement seeks a restored Greater Romania.

natural-rulers.rationale: Codreanu chose his followers rather than being elected; the movement wants moral soldiers as a ruling elite.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Legion glorified sacrifice and used violence, though recent neo-Legionary strategy has moved away from it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Codreanu's death teams and cult of sacrifice treat struggle and death as national regeneration.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement fuses Orthodoxy and state; a call for separation appears in the book only in an opposing 1920 manifesto.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: It wants Orthodox values to shape public life, but a scriptural legal code is not documented.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A nationalist movement with a strong state ideal does not privatize courts or defense.

military-superiority.rationale: The creed makes the army a school of the nation and the movement prizes national strength; the specific goal of superiority is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Neo-Legionarism seeks an ethnically defined nation, listed as a core feature.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The creed seeks harmony and minimizing of class differences, and Noua Dreapta rejects Marxism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The creed narrows class differences but ties pay to work and family size.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; an ethnic-majority nationalism leans against it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to international guilt politics.

civilizational-union.rationale: Noua Dreapta wants Romania-Moldova union and Orthodox solidarity; wider union is inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Sacrifice for the nation is the ethos; Codreanu calls on followers to die for the people.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Human rights are criticized and the Legion demanded sacrifice and discipline.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Folklore mysticism exists but no position on nature's value is documented.

limit-population.rationale: Defending Romanians' numbers against minorities suggests pronatalism; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: It criticizes modernity morally but not industry as such; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Restoration of a past order dominates, so disruptive acceleration is disfavored.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Orthodox religiosity and its ideal of a morally formed new man rather than a technologically altered one.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Personal leadership and spiritual elite are the ideal; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not discussed; a security-minded movement that fears infiltration would likely prefer state access.

restore-past-order.rationale: The interwar era under Codreanu is held up as a golden age to be restored.

results-over-ideology.rationale: It is a doctrinal mystical movement and judges by fidelity to the creed.

direct-action.rationale: Rejects parliaments and used violent demonstrations, though some groups now contest elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Codreanu stressed that the Legion's moral conduct and self-reform must precede changing the nation.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing suggests it; the movement wants an ordered Orthodox nation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The creed keeps workers, tradesmen and national unions organised by occupation, so the division of labour stays.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The creed links pay to both work and number of children, mixing need and effort.

production-for-use.rationale: The creed keeps private initiative and returns to owners, so profit remains.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist theory is rejected, though Jewish finance is blamed for exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Communism is the Church's mortal enemy and Noua Dreapta opposes Marxism.

collective-farming.rationale: The creed distributes land among individual ploughmen and defends the peasant smallholder, not collective farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a Legionary theme; Codreanu blames Jewish power and communism for national ills, not capitalism's imperial dynamics.

taxation-theft.rationale: Codreanu's 1920 creed endorses a progressive income tax, so taxation is treated as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: The movement wants moral legislation against homosexuality, drugs and abortion.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are attached to the nation; human rights discourse is criticized.

conscription.rationale: The creed treats military service as a school of the nation.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Contradicts national attachment and a strong state; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Politics is a moral mission, not a market relationship; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: The creed offers material support but not as a theory of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Codreanu says Jews control press and money; universities are not discussed.

hereditarian-race.rationale: An ethnically defined nation and antisemitism usually rest on inherited traits, though Legionary doctrine is spiritual.

organic-representation.rationale: The creed gives national unions seats on administrative boards and abolishes the Senate for organized representation.

total-state.rationale: It treats politics as a total spiritual struggle with a regeneration of the whole person; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Spiritual revolution and the creation of a new man are central.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Noua Dreapta seeks union with Moldova and revision of Trianon and other losses.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Followers swear loyalty to the Captain, a personal rather than institutional authority.

bound-labor.rationale: The creed gives land to those who plough it rather than binding them to a lord.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The movement claims transcendent truth, not power-relative knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: Orthodox moral truths are held universal, though by revelation more than reason.

single-common-good.rationale: The Legion sees a single national good and calls pluralist parties a curse.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Codreanu's Jewish problem answer is hostile to Jews, and later adherents repeat antisemitic conspiracy; Israel itself is not discussed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Noua Dreapta backs Romanians abroad, including in Moldova and Serbia; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Romanian is a living language and the sources never raise language revival; indifferent.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The creed has worker representation but under national leadership, not company votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: No source discusses school finance; Orthodox schooling might attract support but the question is not addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The sources contain no fiscal-policy doctrine, so there is no basis for a position.

economic-freedom.rationale: Neo-Legionarism rejects capitalism and liberalism as the basis of society, so it does not treat economic freedom as a condition of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Codreanu led by moral example and demanded self-reform before reform of others.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalism and the unification of all Romanians in one state are the defining aims in the sources.

force-without-un.rationale: Hostility to the UN and to international bodies suggests willingness to act without its approval; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement is religious and mystical, built on a revelation to Codreanu.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The creed's social benefits are for Romanians only, since the state is the holder of Romanians and only Romanians.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work-based pay and 'lover of work' in the creed suggest work-linked benefits.

class-collaboration.rationale: The creed's aim is social harmony and cooperation of owners and workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heritage is revered: Codreanu laments the ruin of old Romanian churches and the movement defends tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western and anti-Russian currents both exist; no front stated.

workers-nation.rationale: Codreanu organised national unions of Romanian workers against Marxist internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditional roles are defended, though Codreanu's early creed gave women equal civil rights.

ban-interest.rationale: Hostile to Jewish usury and finance; a legal ban is inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Codreanu calls for removal of Jews from national life; a segregation law is inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This is a Marxist thesis; the movement is anti-communist and sees the state as the nation's instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not discussed; a self-sufficiency-minded nationalism would likely favour domestic production, so inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Adherents want immigrants expelled and treat nation as ethnic, so assimilation is not the main idea.

elite-replacement.rationale: It holds that a hidden network threatens the nation and names African and Muslim immigrants as threats.

proportional-representation.rationale: The movement rejects party politics altogether, and electoral systems are not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Romania's Orthodox destiny is mythologized, though mostly inward.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Neo-Legionaries reject modern gender analysis and defend traditional roles, so they deny that society is structured to advantage men.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Codreanu calls the party system a curse and says parties are tools of Jewish power; elite corruption is a central theme.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No source documents a neo-Legionary stance on eugenic limits on reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Prison-saint narrative demands reckoning for communist-era abuses; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The creed gives the state a wide role in welfare, economy and morals, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: An ethnic nation and Codreanu's concern with Jews suggest it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The movement defines the nation ethnically, treats minorities as threats and is antisemitic, so equal standing is denied.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A socialist-state debate is outside the movement, which rejects socialism and communism outright.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the movement does not engage with settler-colonial analysis.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Unitary state favours one law, but the privileging of Orthodoxy pulls the other way; adherents are not clearly split on it.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Noua Dreapta opposes religious groups other than the Orthodox Church, and neo-Legionaries denounce other faiths as hostile.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu-nationalist issue that has no relevance to Romanian politics; indifferent.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Putting Orthodoxy at the centre of public life is a core aim, so they want religion taught in state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate; the movement rejects socialism, so the claim is not one it would endorse.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority comes from the Captain and the nation's mission, not consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism suggests favouring exports, but no source states it, so inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling immigrants is documented and the creed treats Jews as hostile.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Legion made violence and sacrificial death part of its method, so adherents reject an absolute bar on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement sees history as struggle between good and evil and peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Legionary groups have been targeted by such laws and oppose them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican-theory concept absent from the sources; no position.

separated-powers.rationale: The creed removes the Senate and favors strong centralized leadership.

vanguard-party.rationale: Codreanu's Legion was an elite of moral soldiers leading the masses.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The creed prioritizes peasants and workers, and Codreanu frames the movement as defending them against exploitation.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is not addressed in any source.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: National unions opposed to class struggle imply limits on strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Codreanu blames Jewish exploitation and the party system for peasant poverty, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Minorities and immigrants are framed as threats to national unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Codreanu chose his followers himself and wanted a ruling elite of moral soldiers, the opposite of random selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: An authoritarian movement obsessed with enemies would accept emergency powers; inferred from its outlook.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The creed's storehouses and risk fund show a state-protective economics; price caps are inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Codreanu blames a Jewish-controlled press; control by a nationalist movement is inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Legion wanted the army as a school of nation but no stated party command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Anti-immigration and ethnic nationalism point toward restrictive citizenship rules.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The sources are silent on pay for officeholders.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Codreanu's Legion required strict obedience and he avoided voting.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU is listed as a threat and Noua Dreapta is hard Eurosceptic.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Captain principle concentrates authority in one leader, who would command the armed forces; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The movement is tied to the Orthodox Church with its bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: It is a lay movement with priests as allies, not clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Internationalist class politics is condemned; workers are to organise nationally and support their nation.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Neo-Legionaries campaign against what they call immorality and obscenity; censorship is inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The leader principle implies no limit on a leader's tenure; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources do not address recall elections.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Neo-Legionaries list NATO among threats and oppose it, favouring withdrawal from alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: The creed keeps a standing army that trains conscripts for a year, so it does not replace it with an armed populace.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement idealises the peasant and Orthodox village and laments the decay of cities.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Noua Dreapta supports unifying Moldova with Romania, a central irredentist aim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The creed asks the educated to descend among the tired and humble, implying they are detached from them.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The movement treats the Romanian nation as having a special spiritual destiny and denounces rival cultures as threats.

death-penalty.rationale: A cult of death and punishment of enemies suggests support, though its own martyrs were executed; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Neo-Legionaries oppose LGBT rights and gender equality agendas, so they oppose such school content.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Orthodox religiosity suggests support, though the sources do not discuss evolution; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The movement's moral campaign against immorality makes legal restriction likely; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The creed has a state for Romanians and only Romanians, implying citizenship by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minorities are treated as threats and the state is one of Romanians, so minority-language schooling is not supported.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Noua Dreapta opposes non-Orthodox religious groups, so it would not accommodate them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The movement demands conformity to a disciplined moral order and a single national mould.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The sources never discuss debt cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Neo-Legionaries treat foreign capital and international companies as threats to independence; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Codreanu rejects parliamentary democracy, so a democratically elected assembly is not their route to a constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The sources link no economic developmental goal to restricting freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nation-first outlook and hostility to international bodies make a duty of aid unlikely; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Sovereigntist self-reliance suggests support; the question is not discussed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Codreanu rejected elections and put authority in a chosen leader rather than votes.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The movement is hostile to finance and international institutions, so independence from government is unlikely to be favoured.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Noua Dreapta treats lost territories as Romanian land, which they would not give up.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The creed encourages private initiative in the interest of the nation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Soviet system seen as communist and hostile, not capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not discussed in any source.

collective-defense.rationale: Neo-Legionaries list NATO among threats and oppose it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Northern Bukovina and Bessarabia claims follow from irredentism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Orthodox Church is central and allied to the movement, which would not curb it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Codreanu's leader would be above parties but a partisan movement leader.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The creed demands one undivided state, so force against secession is consistent.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Unitary-state nationalism opposes a region retaining distinct arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Codreanu is venerated as a figure with a revelation, but not as head of state of divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The creed endorses a progressive income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement stresses spiritual calling and the formation of a new man; upbringing is stressed but nature too, so inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Captain is absolute, but adherents hold a moral law above him; split, so neutral.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a priority for an inward-looking, spiritual nationalism; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Codreanu rejects the parliamentary balance of forces and wants unified leadership.

leader-cult.rationale: Codreanu is venerated as Captain and a cult of him persists, as the Wikipedia article documents.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not their framework; they reject socialism entirely.

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1920 creed proposed distributing land among all the ploughmen.

refugee-return.rationale: No source gives a position on refugee return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Noua Dreapta claims Moldova and Trianon territories for Romanians.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not stated; punishment of leaving Orthodoxy is not documented.

women-must-cover.rationale: The movement is traditionalist but Orthodox norms do not require full covering; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Neo-Legionaries are hard Eurosceptic and oppose pooling sovereignty with the EU.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Noua Dreapta seeks Romanian-Moldovan union; broader kin-union is inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minorities are treated as threats, not self-governing cultural communities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Codreanu's solution to the Jewish problem is that they leave, not that they seek equal rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxism is rejected, and the movement reads history as spiritual and national struggle.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in any source.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed by any source.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rejects liberal constraints and favours unified national will; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Neo-Legionaries reject gender equality agendas and defend traditional roles.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The creed's national economy points toward self-sufficiency, but colonial blocs do not apply to Romania; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Opposes international regulation and treaties that bind the nation.

moral-incentives.rationale: Sacrifice for the nation and duty over gain is the Legion's ethos, though the creed also pays wages.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Legion's death teams and revolutionary violence reflect a belief that a small committed group can force change.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The early creed backed King Ferdinand, but titles are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The national myth of a golden age under Codreanu puts the nation at the centre of the story.

patriotic-education.rationale: Reverence for the nation and its symbols is central, so schools should teach pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Ethnic-nationalist, so opposition to minority preferences is inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Hostile to bankers and usury, so public money creation is inferred to be favoured.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not discuss capitalism's crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Romania had no overseas empire; the question is not applicable.

delink-world-market.rationale: The creed has a national economy but not a break with world markets; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that the movement does not hold.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement wants discrimination enforced by the state rather than left to private owners; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights discourse is criticized as a liberal, humanist device.

elective-rulers.rationale: Codreanu rejected elections and chose leaders himself.

minority-veto.rationale: The Legion put unity and discipline above dissent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Legion resisted what it saw as an illegitimate regime, so resistance to a ruler is accepted.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Codreanu rejected parliamentary democracy as a curse.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A traditional rural outlook accepts use of animals, with moderation; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The creed asks educated and better-off Romanians to go among the tired and humble.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Legion made political struggle a sacred duty, not a thing to avoid.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The movement criticizes modern mass culture and media as hostile forces; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis not found in the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Neo-Legionaries attack international companies and foreign capital as exploiting Romania; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: The creed makes the state one of Romanians and only Romanians.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question the movement does not engage with.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: National self-sufficiency and distrust of international bodies suggest support.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Noua Dreapta treats Trianon as incomplete justice and seeks restoration of interwar Greater Romania.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Neo-Legionaries reject the fascism label and see anti-fascism as a communist tool.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: They reject the claim of fascist-communist equivalence because they treat communism as the enemy and their movement as martyrs.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is outside the movement's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Neo-Legionaries campaign to honour Legionary martyrs and resist removal of their monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Traditionalists often hold it, but the sources are silent; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Neo-Legionaries reject liberal-secular humanism and defend an Orthodox civilizational form.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is honoured in the creed; a guardian political role is inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: The sources are silent on wages for care work.

filial-duty.rationale: The movement defends the traditional family as the foundation of the nation.

office-by-exam.rationale: The sources do not discuss examinations for office.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Neo-Legionaries attack international companies and foreign capital.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Orthodox traditionalism would resist easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Captain principle subordinates followers to the leader, not the other way.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions are not addressed in any source.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The creed distributes land to individual ploughmen as holders, not communal tenure.

single-official-language.rationale: The creed envisions one undivided state of Romanians only.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The creed gives land to Romanian ploughmen and treats foreign property as a threat; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Neo-Legionaries reject anti-discrimination and human-rights frameworks.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The movement's ascetic and sacrificial ethos opposes materialism; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The sources do not address this; sovereigntism suggests some opposition.

corporate-influence.rationale: Neo-Legionaries criticize international companies and big money.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The movement attacks human-rights NGOs as agents of hostile forces; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local nationalism favours limiting purchases; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The creed's defence of workers and a risk fund supports job security; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement rejects democracy as a harm, so spreading it is not seen as beneficial.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Legion defied the state yet demanded total obedience from members; adherents reject a general freedom from obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereigntism and hostility to the UN suggest support; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed beyond national syndicates.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Codreanu and Wikipedia document Jews as conspiring against nation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Traditional family is defended by the movement.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The sources are silent on freedom of information.

local-production.rationale: A national-economy ethos suggests it; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Legion was a disciplined hierarchy under a single leader, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereigntist stance against the UN, EU and international bodies.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Sovereigntist stance rejects ritual deference to others.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Unitary-state nationalism opposes regional retention; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The movement rejects Marxism wholesale, including the idea of holding means of production in common.

defeat-communism.rationale: Neo-Legionaries portray communism as the Church's mortal enemy and claim to be the main anti-communist force.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement is built on Orthodox faith and mysticism, so religion is not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The movement rejects capitalism as a basis of society and blames it on Jewish finance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Neo-Legionaries defend traditional roles and reject this Marxist-feminist claim; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: The movement treats the family as foundation and opposes socialising its functions.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic nationalism makes purging likely; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The creed envisages a strong unified state, not small cooperatives.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic nationalism makes settlement of Romanians in minority regions plausible; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Noua Dreapta opposes both Marxism and capitalism and follows a third-position ideology.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Noua Dreapta claims land by history, as with Moldova and Trianon territories.

holocaust-denial.rationale: A prominent neo-Legionary figure publicly denied the Holocaust in 2002, per Veridica; extent among adherents is uncertain.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Neo-Legionaries oppose homosexuality; the sources do not state criminalization, so it is inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement's authoritarianism implies it; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Orthodox-nationalist movement would likely favour penalties; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Specific to Islam; not the movement's framework, and it names Muslims as threats.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not the movement's framework; it prefers Orthodox rule but not armed removal on that basis.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement rejects democracy and rule by assemblies.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Neo-Legionaries reject human-rights and identity-politics frameworks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Neo-Legionaries oppose LGBT rights and gender ideology.

assisted-dying.rationale: Orthodox religion opposes assisted dying; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Third-position movements claim to transcend left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept the movement does not use.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Muslims are named as threats to the nation in the Wikipedia account.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The movement wants Orthodoxy visible in public life; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement rejects capitalism, including its social-market form.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The army is honoured as a school of the nation, so abolishing it is rejected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Neo-Legionaries oppose NATO, suggesting non-alignment; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Captain principle has leaders chosen by merit and revelation rather than inheritance; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Hostile to usury and finance; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sovereigntist and hostile to international financial bodies; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Hegelian concept the movement does not use.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Codreanu says Jews control press and money, so he would agree that wealth controls the presses.

racial-franchise.rationale: The creed gives political life to Romanians only, implying an ethnic franchise.

online-participation.rationale: The movement rejects democracy, so online deliberation is unlikely to appeal.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Codreanu urged Romanians to support Romanian commerce against Jewish shopkeepers; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The movement rejects democratic deliberation as divisive.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement attacks Jewish finance and big money.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Religion is central, so atheist promotion is firmly rejected; Codreanu portrays communist atheism as the Church's enemy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement stresses order and authority.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Unitary-state nationalism favours one national community in power.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not address it.

vote-delegation.rationale: The movement rejects democratic mechanisms generally.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Orthodox tradition excludes women from priestly office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Traditional roles are defended, though the early creed gave women equal civil rights.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement is anti-immigration and wants immigrants expelled.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Legion nests, labour camps and neo-Legionary youth camps train the young in discipline.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Neo-Legionaries oppose NATO, so they oppose foreign bases; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The creed pays by work performed and shrinks owners' returns relative to their investment.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: A movement fixated on the survival of the ethnic Romanian nation and hostile to immigration would prefer native births to immigration; family incentives are inferred, not documented.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not an issue for a Romanian movement; its anti-exploitation, anti-foreign-capital stance suggests it would not endorse economic extraction.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Codreanu credited a revelation from Archangel Michael and the creed pictures a state in fear of God, so authority is framed as ultimately religious.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Codreanu's rule by the Captain's personal choice and judgment, with no committees or votes, sits badly with fixed standing laws; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Prison Saints devotion and Legionary martyr cult make sacrificial death a sacred, public national honour.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Described as viewing politics as a spiritual battle with a revelation from Archangel Michael to Codreanu.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Legionary tradition glorified violence and sacrifice for the nation, so rejecting killing even in defence is contrary to its creed.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Its ethnic nationalism and Greater Romania programme assume the nation as an unbroken organic continuity from ancestors to the present, though the sources state this only implicitly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its Orthodox, traditionalist and ethnic-organic worldview.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its traditional, organic view of the nation and gender roles.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The movement aims to restore Greater Romania so that the Romanian people live in one state, not to serve as a distant centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Codreanu's creed aims first at spiritual rebirth and the moral formation of a new man, with political power following, though the movement also seeks a state.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its intense, traditional Orthodox mysticism.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its intense Orthodox religiosity, which treats tradition as authoritative.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Its ethnic nationalism and antisemitism include demands that Romanians, not minorities such as Jews, control the nation's economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Read literally this concerns internal regions, which the sources do not address; inferred from the aim of a Greater Romania bringing Romanians into one territorial unit.

missingStatements.text: Those who die for the nation should be honoured as martyrs and saints.
missingStatements.rationale: The Prison Saints devotion and Legionary martyr cult make sacrificial death a sacred, public national honour.

missingStatements.text: Politics is fundamentally a spiritual struggle between good and evil.
missingStatements.rationale: Described as viewing politics as a spiritual battle with a revelation from Archangel Michael to Codreanu.

notes: Adherents deny the fascist label and some groups deny the neo-Legionary label (AUR, Georgescu). Economic and many modern-issue answers are inferred from Codreanu's 1920 creed and third-position claims, so confidence is low there.
